question: What claim about the authority of the yoginī named Will is at stake in asserting that she extends to the end of Māyā by supreme will and through the siddhas?
premises: A yoginī named Will is in view.
She extends to the end of Māyā.
This is said to occur by supreme will and by the siddhas.
inference: The yoginī named Will extends to the end of Māyā by supreme will, in relation to the siddhas.
uncertainties: The precise relation between the siddhas and this extension is not specified by this verse alone.
plain_english: The yoginī named Will, by supreme will, extends to the end of Māyā through the siddhas.
